lesson1.description: In this level, you will be learning about the characteristics of good friendships, different types of friendships, and how to trade information in a conversation in order to develop friendships. Trading information is the buzzword that we use for having a good conversation. Good conversations involve the exchanging of information. The most important goal when trading information is to find common interests. Common interests are important because they are the foundation of friendships. These interests are what we talk about with our friends and what we do with our friends. Before reviewing the rules for trading information, it is also helpful to think about the characteristics of good friendships and the different types of friends.
exercises: Review the rules for trading information before practicing
Find common interests
Consider what you could do with that common interest if you were going to hang out with your social coach

lesson2.description: In this level, you will be continuing to learn how to trade information and how to have a two-way conversation with others. Just as in the previous level, there are very specific rules for trading information and having two-way conversations. When talking to others, it is important to share the conversation, so that it goes back and forth from one person to the other. In order to know what to talk about, it can be helpful to think about what people like to talk about with each other.
exercises: Practice trading information with a social coach this week

lesson3.title: Electronic Communication
lesson3.description: In this level you will be learning how to appropriately use electronic forms of communication. There are very specific rules and steps for using electronic communication, which you will be practicing.
exercises: Practice using electronic communication with your social coach
Practice trading information with a social coach this week

lesson4.title: Choosing Appropriate Friends
lesson4.description: In this level, you will be learning how to choose appropriate friends through involvement in extracurricular activities and clubs. The best activities for finding friends are those where there are other people with common interests. This is often done through enrollment in extracurricular activities and finding a social group. Extracurricular activities and choice of social group should be based on your interests. These will be the best methods for meeting potential friends with common interests.
exercises: Enroll in extracurricular activities
Practice using electronic communication with your social coach
Practice trading information with a peer this week

lesson5.description: In this level, we are going to review the rules for appropriate use of humor. Humor is an important way of communicating for many people, and when used appropriately, humor can be very magnetic. However, when humor is used inappropriately it may be one of the fastest ways to push people away. It is important to understand the rules for using humor if you want to make and keep friends.
exercises: Pay Attention to your humor feedback if you happen to tell a joke
Enroll in extracurricular activities
Practice using electronic communication with your social coach
Practice trading information with a peer this week

lesson6.title: Starting and Entering Conversations
lesson6.description: In this level, you will be learning how to start and enter conversations with people you want to know better. When trying to meet new people, we are sometimes given the advice to go up and say"hi" or introduce ourselves - this is bad advice. Simply interrupting to say hello or introduce ourselves would seem odd or random and would likely result in rejection. Instead the rules for starting and entering conversations with casual acquaintances are very specific and are presented below. Although these steps are not required for people we already know well, they can be used when starting or entering conversations with any type of friendship.
exercises: Practice starting an individual conversation and entering a group conversation with peers this week.
Pay attention to your humor feedback if you happen to tell a joke.
Enroll in extra curricular activities.
Practice using electronic communication with your social coach

lesson7.description: In this level you will be learning how to exit conversations. Approximately 50% of attempts to enter conversations are unsuccesful. And that is okay, it happens to everyone and is often not personal. Don't let this stop you from trying to join converations in the future. There are many different reasons why you might not be accepted when you try to join a conversation, it is important to think about why we might have been turned down and what we can do differently next time.
exercises: Practice starting, entering, and exiting conversations with peers this week.
Pay attention to your humor feedback if you happen to tell a joke.
Enroll in extracurricular activites.

lesson8.description: In this level, you will be learning how to be a good sport during games and sports activities. There are very specific rules for being a good sport. The main goal of playing games and sports with friends is that everyone enjoys themselves. That is why it is important that we use good sportsmanship when we play videogames, computer games, board games, or sports. If we use poor sportsmanship while playing games and sports, our friends may no longer want to play with us and we may even get a bad reputation.
exercises: Practice being a good sport.
Practice starting, entering, and exiting conversations with peers this week.
Pay attention to your humor feedback if you happen to tell a joke.
Enroll in extra curricular activities.

lesson9.title: Get-Togethers
lesson9.description: In this level, you will be learning how to have successful get-togethers with perrs. Having get-togethers is an important part of developing friendships. Specific suggestions about how to have a successful get-together are provided below. Get-togethers should be activity based whenever possible to avoid boredom and take the pressure off from having to talk the whole time. Activites should be based on the common interests of everyone.
exercises: Have a get together with a friend
Practice starting, entering, and exiting conversations with peers this week.
Pay attention to your humor feedback if you happen to tell a joke.
Enroll in extra curricular activities.

lesson10.description: In this level, you will be learning about dating etiquette. By now, you've learned some of the basic elements for making and keeping friends. The social skills needed for making and keeping friends are also used in dating. That's because you need to know how to be a friend in order to be more than a friend. The goal of the next several sessions is to provide you with some basic tools for dating that go beyond friendship status. To start we're going to talk about finding and choosing people to date and how to let someone know you like them.
exercises: Practice letting someone know you like them.
Have a get together with a friend.
Practice starting, entering, and exiting conversations with peers this week.
Pay attention to your humor feedback if you happen to tell a joke.

lesson12.description: In this level, you will continue to learn about dating etiquette. So far, you've learned about how to let someone know you like them and how to ask someone out on a date. In this lesson, we're going to talk about going on dates. There are several phases for going on dates, including: planning the date, preparing for the date, staying safe on the date, beginning the date, during the date, ending the date, and after the date. We will talk about what you need to do during each of these phases.
exercises: Practice letting someone know you like them asking them on a date, and/or going on a date.
Practice the following skills for dating etiquette with a social coach
Have a get-together with a friend

lesson14.description: In this level, you will learn how to handle disagreements. Arguments and disagreements with friends or romatical partners are commone, and occasional arguments that aren't too explosive shouldn't have to end your friendship or relationship. Because occasional disagreements are common, it's important to know how to manage them so they don't hurt our friendships or relationships. There are two positions we may find ourselves in when it comes to disagreements. Someone might be upset with us, where we have to RESPOND to a disagreement, or we might be upset with someone, where we have to BRING UP a disagreement.
exercises: Practice handling a disagreement.
Practice letting someone know you like them, asking them on a date, and/or going on a date.
Practice the following skills for dating etiquette with a social coach
Have a get-together with a friend.

lesson15.title: Handling Direct Bullying
example_videos: PeersVideosContent/topic_15/videos/PEERS - Handling teasing - Having an attitude.mp4
lesson15.description: In this level, you will learn how to handle direct bullying. We know bullying is very common among adolescents, and unfortunately it also happens with adults. This level will provide strategies for handling DIRECT bullying, such as teasing and physical bullying because they happen directly to the person targeted and not over the internet or behind their back. In the next level, you will learn about handling indirect forms of bullying, such as cyberbullying, rumors, and gossip.
exercises: Practice handling a disagreement.
Practice letting someone know you like them, asking them on a date, and/or going on a date.
Practice the following skills for dating etiquette with a social coach
Have a get-together with a friend.

lesson16.description: In this level, you will learn how to handle INDIRECT forms of bullying, such as cyberbullying, rumors, and gossip. These are INDIRECT forms of bullying because they usually happen over the internet or behind our back. Just like bullying behaviors are completely different, the strategies for handling these different types of bullying are also very different.
exercises: Practice handling a disagreement.
Practice letting someone know you like them, asking them on a date, and/or going on a date.
Practice the following skills for dating etiquette with a social coach
Have a get-together with a friend.

lesson17.title: Final Review
lesson17.description: In this level, you will be given suggestions about where to go from here. Feel free to refer back to the previous levels to refresh your memory about the strategies for making and keeping friends, dating etiquette, and handling conflict and rejection. Like any newly learned skills, the strategies taught in PEERS require lots of rehearsals, so don't forget to keep practicing!
